newsitem.title: USA: Continental Air pilots push wage demands.
newsitem.headline: Continental Air pilots push wage demands.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc's pilots union said it is looking for hefty wage increases as it heads into negotiations on a new labor contract.

Capt. Bill Borrelli, vice president of the Independent Association of Continental Pilots (IACP), said the carrier had completed a successful turnaround and is now making strong profits, so it needs to sharply increase pilots' pay.
"It is time for Continental management to make good with the Continental pilots. We are going to hold their feet to the fire on that issue," Borrelli told reporters on a conference call.
Borrelli said the union's 4,900 pilots are paid about 35 percent less than their peers at rival airlines because of concessions offered when the carrier came close to collapse.
He refused to say exactly how much the IACP would demand once wage negotiations began in April, but said pilots want the wage gap to be made up quickly.

"They (management) took it when they needed it, and they took it immediately. The company has made a remarkable and dramatic turnaround; the pilots clearly shared in part of that success, and it is time for management to belly up to the bar, sooner rather than later," Borrelli said.

Borrelli said "Management remarked that we were able to make this huge leap from bottom of the industry to top of the industry in just a year. It seems to me we shouldn't have to wait very long now, should we?"

Continental earlier said its fourth-quarter earnings rose to $47 million, or $0.61 a share fully diluted, from $41 million in the year-earlier period. Borrelli said the airline's executives are the best in the industry and the pilots union had "no intention" of hurting the carrier.
Chairman Gordon Bethune earlier said he expects to reach a new labor pact which offers increased compensation, but did not detail what management plans to offer.
"Pilots deserve what's fair for the pilots ... I see no reason to have acrimony, disruption and heartburn," he said on a separate conference call.
Continental's pilots have a history of difficult relations with the airline since former chairman Frank Lorenzo put it into bankruptcy in 1983 and rescinded its labor agreements.
But union leaders have approved of Bethune's efforts to turn the company around.

Borrelli said the pilots' union would be open to discussing profit-sharing schemes and taking an equity stake in the airline as part of contract negotiations, but he insisted that the principal issue would be pay.
